newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: NATO says will remain open for new members.
newsitem.headline: NATO says will remain open for new members.

text.p: A top official of the North Atlantic Treaty Organisation (NATO) said on Friday the defence alliance would remain open for new members beyond its first wave of enlargement expected in 1999.

"The opening of NATO is a process. NATO's door will remain open for others to join. Madrid should not therefore be seen as a definitive day of judgement," Norman Ray, NATO's Assistant Secretary General said in a speech at a high-level conference on Central-Eastern Europe and Euro-Atlantic Security.
The 16-member NATO is expected to invite several former East bloc states to start negotiations on full membership at its summit in Madrid on July 7 and 8.
The Czech Republic, Poland and Hungary are seen to be the most likely candidates, while Slovenia and Romania are also seen as potential members.

"The decision on who will be the first new members is yet to be made. The Secretary General expects that the decision will be made as a result of intense consultations among the Allies in the immediate run-up to Madrid," Ray said.
